ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (InfernalBlade.cs:15-18) == cost 1 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / SELF.

OnPlay.rationale: THE STREAM IS HANDLED CORRECTLY HERE, and this is the pattern the other generation cards need. C# is `CardFactory.GetDistinctForCombat(Owner, characterPool.Where(c => c.Type == Attack), 1, Owner.RunState.Rng.CombatCardGeneration)` then `SetToFreeThisTurn()` then `AddGeneratedCardToCombat(cardModel, PileType.Hand, Owner)` (InfernalBlade.cs:22-29). The sim branches on `crng.is_parity` and calls `get_distinct_for_combat_parity(crng.card_gen, 1, CardType.ATTACK)` (infernal_blade.py:203-205), keeping the shared legacy rng only for non-parity RL runs (207-209) -- exactly what card/discovery, card/distraction, card/jack_of_all_trades, card/jackpot and card/hidden_gem fail to do. The free-this-turn-then-add order matches, and `set_free_this_turn` is cleared by the turn-start reset (cards/base.py:265-269) like C#'s EndOfTurn expiration. The C# filter is the CHARACTER pool restricted to Attacks; `random_pool_cards`/`get_distinct_for_combat_parity` default to IRONCLAD_POOL, the same membership.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `EnergyCost.UpgradeBy(-1)` (InfernalBlade.cs:34) == `self._energy_cost -= 1` (1 -> 0). No clamp is needed at this base cost, so the missing `max(0, ...)` other cards use is harmless here.
